findings.description: The grader_versions tally is sorted with a key that splits each grade.json grader_version on '.' and converts digit-only parts with int(). grader_version is read verbatim from grade.json files in the run directories (untrusted batch-record data). Two distinct versions in one batch whose parts mix types, e.g. "1.2" and "1.b", produce the key lists [1, 2] and [1, "b"]; sorting compares 2 with "b" and raises TypeError. A part such as "²" passes str.isdigit() but int() raises ValueError. Neither exception is caught (the try/except only wraps open/json.load), so the whole report aborts with a traceback, even though the header and docstring promise the batch record is read-only and "never fatal". The same pattern (isdigit() then int()) is used for version ordering at line 840 and for primary_suite_version in the JSON.
findings.failure_mode: A single malformed or hostile grade.json in any run directory (which the evaluated agent may be able to influence) stops report generation for the entire suite, including the pre-registered decisions, with an unhandled exception instead of the documented exit 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Sort grader versions with a type-stable key, e.g. tuple((0, int(p)) if p.isdigit() and p.isascii() else (1, p) for p in parts), and wrap the whole per-version computation so malformed values fall into the "n/a" bucket; apply the same guard to version_order/version_key and to the primary_suite_version conversion.

findings.description: batch_record builds the run-directory path as os.path.join(d, r["arm"]) where r["arm"] comes from a runs.jsonl row. The report does not re-check the arm grammar (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ is enforced only by ablation-row.sh --validate, which is optional and runs at write time). An arm value containing '../' segments or an absolute path makes os.listdir and the subsequent grade.json reads operate outside the batch directory. Only directories matching <task_id>-t<trial>[-r<k>] are opened and only grader_version is extracted, so disclosure is limited to that string, but the traversal itself is unconstrained.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted row can steer the report to list arbitrary directories and read arbitrary grade.json files anywhere the reporting user can access, leaking their grader_version into the published report and bypassing the intended <batch dir>/<arm>/ containment.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate r["arm"] against the arm grammar (or require it to be a key of suite arms) before joining, and additionally assert os.path.realpath(ad) is inside os.path.realpath(d) before listing.

findings.description: version_key strips and normalises row suite_version strings, matching \d+ with re.fullmatch and converting with int(). version_order then calls k.isdigit() and int(k) again. str.isdigit() accepts characters like '²' that int() rejects, and int() rejects decimal strings longer than Python's 4300-digit limit even though \d+ matches them. A row carrying such a suite_version raises ValueError outside the Fail handler, so the report dies with a traceback instead of the documented exit 2.
findings.failure_mode: One malformed row in runs.jsonl aborts report generation for every suite version with an unhandled exception.
findings.suggested_fix: Use re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", s) (ASCII only) with a length cap, and make version_order rely on the same predicate; catch ValueError and raise Fail naming the row.

findings.description: The new per-version sections and the budget-matched table interpolate row-derived strings directly into Markdown: the suite_version key v goes into '## Suite version {v} …' headers and bullet lines, and e['task_id'] goes into the budget table cells without md_cell(). version_key only strips outer whitespace, so a suite_version such as "1\n**H1: established**" or a task_id containing '|' can inject fake lines or break table structure in a report whose purpose is a pre-registered, human-read decision record. Other new fields (STATUS.json state, cuts, extra_models, grader versions) are correctly passed through md_cell.
findings.failure_mode: A tampered row can spoof decision text or corrupt tables in report.md while report.json stays consistent, misleading a reader who only sees the Markdown.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject suite_version values containing control characters in version_key, and wrap v and task_id in md_cell() (or a header-safe variant) wherever they are rendered.

findings.description: The STATUS.json reader (and the grade.json reader at lines 1072-1075) implements the documented 'a symlink is not read' control as os.path.islink() followed by a separate open(). The check and the open are not atomic, so a path swapped to a symlink between them is followed. The control is therefore advisory only.
findings.failure_mode: A concurrent writer in the batch directory can make the reporter read an arbitrary JSON file through a symlink despite the stated guarantee; impact is limited to the fields the report extracts.
findings.suggested_fix: Open with os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW) and os.fdopen, or fstat the opened descriptor and compare to lstat before parsing.
